boards.name: AM HATSU
boards.description: Wireless split ergonomic board, 4x6 layout, BLE 5.0, two 5,000 mAh batteries, 3 W Qi charging. 3D-curved metal halves, combined weight 1.54 kg. Two supported layers, white PCB lighting, proprietary low-frequency inter-half link.

evidence: Official 4x6 / 45% split ortho description. Scene uses two 4x6 1u halves with a gap; not manufacturer CAD, tent angle, or half footprint.

boards.notes: HATSU-to-CYBERMAT R2 compatibility is official (ten central coils designed for HATSU). Qi placement unverified without footprint.

boards.name: CYBERBOARD R2
boards.description: 75%-class board with 5 x 40 LED panel, 200 screen LEDs + 81 in-switch LEDs, BLE 5.0 + USB-C, Qi charging, 10-degree typing incline, gasket mount, hot-swap. Manual confirms R2/R3 shared controls.

evidence: Official 5x40 / 200-LED panel count. Scene keeps a generic 75% key grid and adds an illustrative panel; exterior dimensions and LED pitch unpublished.

boards.notes: 40x5 RGB matrix is demonstrable; case silhouette must remain approximate until licensed dimensioned source appears.

boards.name: AM AFA R2
boards.description: Ergonomic Alice-style 65%; Macross-inspired sculptural case. Sold out / limited.

evidence: No CAD or measurement published for this model.

boards.name: AM Relic 80
boards.description: 80% chalk-white or raw collector finish. Current listing; stock varies.

evidence: No CAD or dimensioned source found.

boards.name: CYBERBOARD R3
boards.description: 75% gasket mount; upgraded LED matrix with higher refresh/color reproduction; 256-level DC dimming; shared R2/R3 manual confirms same control family.

evidence: No official CAD or dimensions published; R3 manual shared with R2.

boards.name: CYBERBOARD Terminal
boards.description: 75% retro-futuristic RGB; translucent integrated gasket mount; mirror-PVD stainless weight. Engraved bundle $810 / base kit $528; both sold out.

evidence: No CAD published; distinctive retro-futuristic profile.

boards.name: AM Neon 80
boards.description: 80% synthwave design, four-dimensional RGB matrix lighting, three-stage leaf spring. Product page current; no verified price.

boards.name: AM RGB 65 R1.5
boards.description: 65% Game Boy-inspired DIY LED panel, adjustable leaf-spring mount. Limited / sold out variants; from $435 (regular $451).

boards.name: the Seneca
boards.description: Electrocapacitive board sold as the First Edition. Plasma-ceramic finished aluminium in Oxide Gray, Travertine or Heatshield, or bead-blasted Veracity Titanium, with a thick solid brass switch plate in matte silver chrome. Ships with an MTNU-profile R&D 1973 double-shot PBT set moulded by GMK. Designed for a flat typing position; an optional CNC walnut riser adds a 3 degree pitch.

offers.configuration: First Edition, lowest listed configuration of a $3,900-$8,900 range

evidence: No CAD or dimensioned drawing published; the listing describes finishes and materials only.

boards.notes: The listing publishes only the endpoints of its price range, so the lowest is recorded and the configuration reaching $8,900 is not attributed here. Sold out for immediate shipment: a 10 percent nonrefundable deposit reserves a build slot, and the listing states a nine-month queue estimate.

boards.name: Sonnet
boards.description: 75% kit measuring 315 x 143 mm with a 19 mm front height, 24 mm back height and 5.5 degree typing angle, assembling to 4-7.5 lb. Media-blasted aluminium top and bottom with a maple accent and a stainless steel weight. The base kit is the case, PCB and daughterboard, mounting system, feet and fasteners; switches, keycaps and stabilisers are bought separately. QMK/VIA ARM PCB for 80-83 MX-style switches.

offers.configuration: Base kit, before edition, PCB and plate options

evidence: Case measurements are published, but no CAD or plate/PCB geometry is.

boards.notes: Priced from $289 with per-option costs added at build time (edition +$30 or +$40, hot-swap PCB +$5, plate +$10 to +$40), so an assembled price depends on choices not recorded here. Black Sesame, Forest Mocha and Steel Mushroom editions were sold out when observed.

boards.name: Encore
boards.description: 65% kit measuring 326 x 125 mm with a 12.5 mm front height (19.7 mm at the chamfer) and a 5.5 degree typing angle, assembling to 2.9-3.2 lb. Crown mounting system, with a media-blasted maple or aluminium top over a media-blasted aluminium middle and bottom on silicone feet. The base kit is the chassis, PCB and daughterboard, mounting system, feet, fasteners, assembly tools and a microsuede bag; switches, keycaps and stabilisers are bought separately. QMK/VIA ARM PCB for 66-68 MX-style switches over USB-C, designed by Gondolindrim.

offers.configuration: Base kit, before plate, switch, stabiliser and keycap options

evidence: Case measurements and typing angle are published, but no CAD or plate/PCB geometry is.

boards.notes: Priced from $299 with options added at build time (carbon fibre or aluminium plate +$10, copper +$40, switches $42 to $50, stabilisers $15, keycaps $59.99), so an assembled price depends on choices not recorded here. Only the Studio Light edition was orderable when observed; Black Sesame, Matcha Cream, Mocha Mushroom and Monterey Dune were sold out, as were the POM plate and the Obscura Linear switches.

boards.name: Chimera65 Round 2
boards.description: 65% kit designed by UPAS and produced with the manufacturer Hongtu, built from seven CNC case parts (top, bottom, weight, back accent, bottom accent, badge and plate) on a Poron gasket isolation sandwich mount. 7.5 degree typing angle, 10.86 mm ledge front height and 17.86 mm front height excluding the ledge; built weight is 1.0 kg in polycarbonate, 2.0 kg for the aluminium Standard edition and 2.2 kg for the Special edition. QMK/VIA STM32 PCB in solder or hot-swap form with a C4 unified daughterboard, shipping with a universal ISO-compatible plate, an aluminium Chimera keycap, carrying case and authenticity card. Switches, keycaps and stabilisers are bought separately.

offers.configuration: Listed price before edition, PCB and stock-grade selection

evidence: Typing angle, front heights and built weights are published; case footprint and plate/PCB geometry are not.

boards.notes: Sold as one listing across eleven colourways in five editions (Standard, PC, E-White, Special and Legendary) and three stock grades, so the single listed price is recorded rather than a per-edition price. The same page still carries provisional group-buy pricing from the 2023 round ($450 Standard, $470 PC and E-White, $630 Special); that is not the current listed price and is not recorded as an offer. Stock was limited when observed. CannonKeys names this and the Satisfaction75 as its premium line, above the Brutal series.

boards.name: Q1 Max
boards.description: 75% board measuring 327.5 x 145 mm with a 20.7 mm front height and 31.8 mm back height excluding keycaps, 2.4 mm feet and a 5.2 degree typing angle, weighing 1724 g plus or minus 10 g fully assembled. CNC-machined 6063 aluminium body on a double-gasket mount, pairing plate gaskets with silicone pads between the top and bottom cases, over a polycarbonate plate. Screw-in PCB stabilisers, south-facing RGB and hot-swap sockets for 3-pin and 5-pin MX-style switches. An ARM Cortex-M4 STM32F402 with 256 KB of flash runs QMK and is remapped through Keychron's Launcher web app. Connects over 2.4 GHz and USB-C at a 1000 Hz polling rate or Bluetooth 5.1 to three devices at 90 Hz, on a 4000 mAh battery rated up to 180 hours with the backlight off.

offers.configuration: Fully assembled with knob, before colour and switch selection

evidence: Case footprint, front and back heights, typing angle and assembled weight are published on the product page.
The studio draws a shared 75% study rather than Keychron case geometry; only the encoder knob is built from published millimetres.

boards.notes: Listed at $209.99 against a $229.99 compare-at price when observed. A Barebone variant without keycaps and switches is sold on the same listing, but the page does not show its price, so it is not recorded as a kit offer. Carbon Black, Shell White and Purple are colourways of one model, and the ISO layouts are a separate collection rather than separate models.

boards.name: Neo75
boards.description: 75% kit measuring 317.4 x 133.8 mm with a 17.6 mm front height and a 7 degree typing angle. Poron gasket mount built on a grooved, adhesive-free gasket structure carried over from the Neo80 Cu, with a chamber-segmented bottom case to break up cavity resonance and a forcebreak layer between the top and bottom cases. Case-only weight is 1459 g with the tri-mode PCB or 1589 g wired. Mirror-polished stainless steel badge, with a stainless steel weight offered in spray-coated or mirror PVD finishes. Hot-swap QMK/VIA PCB in wired ANSI, tri-mode ANSI or tri-mode ISO form over an aluminium or PP plate; tri-mode kits ship with two 2200 mAh batteries and a 2.4 GHz dongle. Switches and keycaps are bought separately.

offers.configuration: Barebone kit, before case colour, weight, PCB and plate selection

evidence: Case footprint, front height, typing angle and case weights are published; plate and PCB geometry are not.

boards.notes: Sold as a pre-order with an estimated six-week fulfilment time when observed, and marked a final-sale item. Seven case colours, five weight finishes, three PCBs and two plate materials are selectors on one listing that shows a single price, so that price is recorded rather than a per-configuration one. A prebuilt version exists whose accessories are not compatible with the barebone kit, and its price is not on this page. Regional vendors resell the kit at prices not recorded here.

boards.name: Ikki68 Aurora
boards.description: 65% kit with a frosted, injection-moulded polycarbonate case measuring 13.6 x 4.4 inches with a 0.9 inch base height excluding rubber feet and a 6.5 degree typing angle, assembling to 800 g or 1120 g with the optional weight. Variable gasket mount whose gasket chips can be removed to move the board from firm to bouncy, shipping with both silicone and Poron gaskets. Anodised aluminium plate by default over the multi-layout hot-swap Fairbanks PCB running QMK/VIA, which supports split left shift, split right shift, split backspace, stepped caps lock and ISO enter without soldering. Badges are hot-swappable without opening the case, and a cutout above the right arrow key is lit from beneath for custom logo chips. Switches and keycaps are bought separately.

offers.configuration: Kit as listed, before colour and wired or wireless PCB selection

evidence: Case dimensions, typing angle and assembled weights are published; plate and PCB geometry are not.

boards.notes: Sold out when observed, so $129 is the last published listing price rather than an orderable one. Charcoal, Mint and the Aurora x Mizu edition are colourways of one model on a single listing, and wired and wireless are PCB options rather than separate models. Wireless editions need a standard LiPo battery that the kit does not include. The listing still carries its 2021 group-buy dates.

boards.name: No. 1/65
boards.description: 65% kit at an 8 degree typing angle, with a 6063 aluminium top, bottom and accent piece in an isolated gasket sandwich mount. The switch plate is a leaf spring design, seated on PTFE plate-alignment pins. The kit takes the VIA-compatible WT65-G solderable or WT65-H1 hot-swap PCB with a USB-C daughterboard designed by wilba.tech. Boxed contents are the chassis, plate, PCB, vibration-damping gaskets, bumpon feet, case screws, hex drivers and the alignment pins. Switches and keycaps are bought separately.

offers.configuration: A-stock kit, in one of three colour combinations: anodized black and gold, rose gold and charcoal, or green and black
B-stock kit, same three colour combinations

evidence: Form factor and typing angle are published; case dimensions, weight and plate geometry are not.

boards.notes: The three colour combinations are one listing at one price, so they are recorded as configurations of a single model rather than separate boards. A-stock and B-stock are separate prices on that listing and are both recorded; the listing does not say what makes a unit B-stock beyond pointing at the maker's quality disclosure. A matching wrist rest and spare switch plates are sold as separate products and are not counted here.

boards.name: No. 2/65
boards.description: 65% kit at an 8 degree typing angle, described by the maker as the first Keycult kit manufactured in-house at its workshop and finished in the USA. Three-part case with hidden-screw construction: powder-coated white top, matte silver anodized middle and an unfinished silver anodized bottom, in an isolated gasket sandwich mount. Silver anodized aluminium leaf spring switch plate on PTFE alignment pins. The kit takes the VIA-compatible WT65-G solderable or WT65-H1 hot-swap PCB with a USB-C daughterboard designed by wilba.tech, though this batch shipped with the solderable PCB only. Switches and keycaps are bought separately.

offers.configuration: A-stock kit, in powder white with unfinished silver or matte anodized blue with unfinished silver
B-stock kit, same two colour combinations

evidence: Form factor, typing angle and case construction are published; case dimensions, weight and plate geometry are not.

boards.notes: Every variant on the listing read as out of stock when observed. The maker sells these in batches by raffle and states the next draw date on the page, so the recorded price is what a winning entrant pays rather than a price anyone can pay on the day. Later revisions and colourways of the No. 2 are separate listings at other prices and are not recorded here.
